scene: At a home kitchen table, Mom sits screen-left and Child screen-right. Child is the four-year-old tiger boy and keeps his yellow T-shirt throughout. One empty transparent cup stands at table-center within both characters' reach. A small open milk pitcher stands just left of the cup and a small open clear-water pitcher farther left, both within Mom's easy reach. Keep these two drinks distinct and show only one cup. The cup stays visibly empty until the final pour; no milk is ever poured, discarded or replaced. Use a locked 16:9 medium two-shot with both faces, hands, the cup and pitcher spouts visible.

emotion.baseline: Calm, warm and regulated baseline. Mom and Child are attentive and relaxed, speaking at normal family conversation volume with small, proportionate facial movements.
emotion.allowed_shift: Child has a brief thoughtful pause before changing his choice, then quiet contentment and a small pleased smile about the park race. Mom responds with ordinary, patient acceptance and a warm confirming nod.
emotion.forbidden: No exaggerated surprise, bouncing, frustration, scolding, dramatic pleading, raised voices or sudden grabbing. Keep the change of mind small and everyday.

clips.start: The cup at center is empty; the milk and water pitchers stand upright on its left; Mom and Child have empty hands.
clips.action: Mom indicates the two pitchers during her question. Child chooses milk while looking at Mom. During her acknowledgment she lifts the milk pitcher with her right hand and brings it beside the cup, keeping the pitcher upright and its spout away from the rim. No liquid flows.
clips.end: Mom holds the milk pitcher upright in her right hand just left of the visibly empty cup; the water pitcher stands farther left; Child waits with empty hands.

clips.start: Mom holds the milk pitcher upright in her right hand just left of the visibly empty cup; the water pitcher stands farther left; Child waits with empty hands.
clips.action: Child briefly glances toward the water, then changes his choice aloud before any pouring. Mom stops, sets the milk pitcher back in its original place, and asks about his running. Child tells her about the park and the race to the big tree with small relaxed gestures. Mom then lifts the water pitcher with her left hand and brings it upright beside the cup. The cup stays visibly empty throughout this clip.
clips.end: Mom holds the water pitcher upright in her left hand beside the still-empty cup; the milk pitcher stands in its original place just left of the cup; Child waits with empty hands.

clips.start: Mom holds the water pitcher upright in her left hand beside the still-empty cup; the milk pitcher stands in its original place just left of the cup; Child waits with empty hands.
clips.action: With water confirmed, Mom pours a generous amount of clear water, sets the water pitcher back farther left, and slides the cup toward Child during her line. Child receives it with both hands, looks at the water level and thanks her with a small smile. Keep the cup below his face during speech, with no drinking until the dialogue ends.
clips.end: Child holds the cup containing clear water; both pitchers stand upright in their original left-side positions; no milk entered the cup.
